description:
AUDITED at origin/main a3a9761d1209165e5230625b9347cf6b0ad09b83
(2026-09-02).

STATUS: LIVE, but the original static reproducer is obsolete.

WHAT CHANGED

fz-kdt.127.2 (29b07acfa, present in the squashed main tree) changed
forwarder key erasure to drop a closure's BRAND while retaining its
CAPTURE TYPES. Therefore the ticket's original calls

  P.run(P.mk(%{a: 1}), 10)
  P.run(P.mk(%{a: 0.5}), 10)

are now separated statically by activation keys:

  P.run/2[closure[?](%{:a => int}), int]
  P.run/2[closure[?](%{:a => float}), int]

Fresh result for the original source:

  Elixir:  12 / 11.0
  interp:  rc 0, 12 / 11.0
  JIT:     rc 0, 12 / 11.0
  AOT:     build rc 0; executable rc 0, 12 / 11.0

The current regression
`compiler2_a_forwarded_lambdas_capture_layout_is_the_static_key`
also passes and pins that static-key behavior.

LIVE REPRODUCER

A mailbox-derived branch prevents the caller from statically knowing
which closure it has, forcing runtime dispatch between the two
map-capture layouts:

  defmodule P do
    fn twice(f, x), do: f.(f.(x))
    fn run(f, x), do: twice(f, x)
    fn mk(m) do
      fn (n) ->
        case m do
          %{a: v} -> n + v
          _ -> n
        end
      end
    end
  end

  fn main() do
    send(self(), 1)
    n = receive do v -> v end

    f = case n > 0 do
      true -> P.mk(%{a: 0.5})
      _ -> P.mk(%{a: 1})
    end
    dbg(P.run(f, 10))

    g = case n < 0 do
      true -> P.mk(%{a: 0.5})
      _ -> P.mk(%{a: 1})
    end
    dbg(P.run(g, 10))
  end

Elixir oracle:

  11.0
  12

MEASURED AT a3a9761d1

  interp: rc 0
          11.0
          12.0                    WRONG second line

  JIT:    rc 134 after printing 11.0
          fz_ref_load_float:
          ExpectedTag { expected: ValueKind(14), found: ValueKind(13) }

  AOT:    build rc 0
          executable rc 134 after printing 11.0
          same fz_ref_load_float ExpectedTag abort

Swapping the int/float maps so the int construction arrives first gives
the symmetric result:

  interp: rc 1 after printing 12
          "extern integer arg must be Int"

  JIT:    rc 134 after printing 12
          fz_ref_load_int:
          ExpectedTag { expected: ValueKind(13), found: ValueKind(14) }

  AOT:    build rc 0; executable rc 134 after printing 12
          same fz_ref_load_int ExpectedTag abort

CURRENT MECHANISM

The compiler correctly creates separate `P.run/2` bodies for
`%{a: int}` and `%{a: float}`, but the dynamic caller must dispatch
between them. Its backend plan contains two questions:

  closure[P.mk lambda](%{:a => float})
  closure[P.mk lambda](%{:a => int})

The callable axis compares construction shapes capture-by-capture.
However, `RuntimeTestAxis::Maps` is explicitly `Erasing`: its runtime
predicate checks only MAP kind, never keys or value types. Therefore
the two capture questions both admit both construction annotations.
Whichever arm arrived first receives both values, sending one closure
to a body grounded for the other capture layout.

This is the source-level instance of fz-kdt.131's surface-coverage law.
Current code and tests explicitly preserve maps among the remaining
runtime-indistinguishable kinds:
`RuntimeTestAxis::precision`, `CallableShape::erasing_overlap`, and
`runtime_indistinguishable_arms_keep_the_order_they_arrived_in`.

REQUIRED FIX

Restore the invariant that every value admitted by a runtime-dispatch
arm is safe for the body behind that arm. For map captures, either:

  * make the relevant map-content distinction runtime-answerable; or
  * do not retain body specializations whose distinction depends on
    map contents the runtime predicate erases.

Do not solve this by choosing a different arm order: both arrival
orders are observably unsound.

ACCEPTANCE / TESTS

1. Add a three-door behavioral fixture with an Elixir oracle for the
   mailbox-driven reproducer.
2. Exercise both int-first and float-first arrival orders; require exact
   outputs `12 / 11.0` and `11.0 / 12`.
3. Pin the callable-axis/map-capture plan so incompatible bodies cannot
   remain distinguishable only in semantic information the runtime
   test erases.
4. Preserve
   `compiler2_a_forwarded_lambdas_capture_layout_is_the_static_key`:
   statically known captures must remain key-separated with no
   manufactured runtime dispatch.
5. Run the focused unit tests, all three fixture lanes, `cargo fmt
   --check`, clippy with warnings denied, `cargo test --lib`, and the
   fixture matrix.

AUDIT CHECKS

  cargo test --release --lib \
    compiler2_a_forwarded_lambdas_capture_layout_is_the_static_key
    -> 1 passed

  cargo test --release --lib \
    runtime_indistinguishable_arms_keep_the_order_they_arrived_in
    -> 1 passed

  cargo test --release --lib \
    the_callable_axis_erases_exactly_where_its_captures_do
    -> 1 passed

Checkout remained detached at a3a9761d1 with no tracked edits.
title: Dynamic same-lambda map captures are runtime-indistinguishable: interpreter misroutes int/float bodies; JIT/AOT abort
